label: paragraph_title
text: BOLSHEVIST ACTIVITY.

label: text
text: Prominence is given in the Indian papers to a question in the House of Commons on July 12 when Sir William Davison asked what action the Government of India was taking with reference to the Bolshevik activity in Afghanistan where, according to the statement "of Colonel M. Saunders," the Director of Military Intelligence in India, an Afghan Air Force was being formed with Russian pilots and mechanics, and also new aerodromes and new military roads and railways. Commander Kenworthy asked whether this was a proper question seeing that Afghanistan was an independent friendly State which was represented at the Court of St. James. Sir William rejoined that surely the Commons was entitled to enquire with regard to a report by a British official. Earl Winterton replied that Lord Birkenhead was enquiring by whose authority the published statement was made, and added that the Government was carefully watching the situation in Afghanistan.

label: text
text: For the benefit of those of our readers who have not fully appreciated the magnitude of Moscow's machinations and the subtlety of detail underlying her campaign against Britain and ultimately against civilisation as a whole, it may be well to quote from the Rangoon Times some of Gol. Saunders's revelations, which were first given to the public at the Saturday Club in Calcutta. The most significant of the Colonel's

label: text
text: statements may come as a shock to the many who still believe that in cultivating friendly relations with the Soviet the British Empire would be taking the most practical step towards the institution of a permanent world peace. Yet it has been amply proved by the speeches and writings of almost every Bolshevik leader who has given his attention to international affairs that "The Third International has declared war on the British Empire." To quote Zinovieff, "Our first weapon is propaganda and our second, force of arms. The Achilles heel of the British Empire is India." We must therefore make every effort to develop all possible lines of advance leading on India." In a later speech he added: "What we planned for India has come to pass in China, but we have hopes that India may make up leeway in a sudden and unexpected fashion."

label: text
text: In addition the Soviet aims at the absorption of Afghanistan. Large subsidies, mostly in the form of arms and munitions, have been given to the Afghans. The Afghan Air Force, with Russian pilots and mechanics, is being developed. It has its main aerodrome at Kabul, and landing grounds have already been made at Kandahar and Jellalabad besides those on the Termez-Kabul air route. From their present aerodromes, therefore, Russians can bomb the Indian frontier stations. The great barrier of the mountains of the North-West Frontier, so long thought to be impregnable to Russian invasion, has been metaphorically razed to the ground by aerial development and the attack on India has at last become a possibility.

label: text
text:
It is a fact; declares Col. Saunders, that the Red Army is a more efficient fighting force than the pre-war Russian Army. It is well equipped with mechanical weapons, and great stress is laid on the use of tanks, armoured cars, aeroplanes, gas and chemical warfare. The Red Army has a large and efficient air force. It is worth noting that, whereas other nations are economising on military expenditure, the Soviet this year is increasing its military budget by fifty per cent.
These are striking disclosures, and it is little cause for wonder that the movement against Bolshevism has taken concrete shape in Shanghai, for instance, and that in Great Britain itself the popular clamour is increasing for the expulsion of the “Red” aliens, whose presence there is a perpetual menace to the whole Empire.

text: [To the Editor of the "China Mail"]

label: text
text: Sir,—The local representative of the Federation of British Industries referred, in your correspondence columns last week to "the thoroughness of British ex-

label: text

label: text
text: Every so often this London paper causes a number of specimen copies to be circulated through the Dominions and Colonies and several hundred, I believe, find their way to Hongkong. text: AJIN OMOTO

label: paragraph_title
text: ALLEGED MISUSE OF TRADE CHOP.

label: text
text: CHINESE SUMMONED.

label: text
text: Three Chinese firms were summoned before Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy yester-day for alleged infringement of the “Ajinomoto” trade mark, the property of Suzuki and Company, Tokyo, and used by them on an epicurian powder.

label: text
text: Mr. L. R. Andrewes represented the Hachiji Imura firm, of Praya East, the sole agents for the manufacturers and complaints in the summonses.

label: text
text: The case against the Yuen Hop firm was taken first. The defendants, who were represented by Mr. D. McCallum, were charged with selling, or having in their possession for sale, powder bearing a forged trade mark.

label: text
text: A representative of the Japanese firm gave evidence of a verbal agreement whereby sub-agents were supplied with goods at a cheaper rate. He said that investigations were made on instructions received that the firm's labels were being forged and the powder sold in Formosa, Certain illegitimate goods were found in the possession of the defendants, who claimed to be unable to differentiate between the forged and genuine labels. Witness further stated that he had not supplied the defendants with any goods for the past one year, but one tin of genuine powder was found among the forged tins.

label: text
text: The defendants were fined $25, the other two summons being adjourned.

label: paragraph_title
text: IRREGULAR?

label: text

label: text
text: MOTORIST'S POSITION.

label: text
text: When summoned before Mr. J. H. B. Nihill, at the Kowloon Magistracy yesterday for driving a car without a licence, Mr. C. M. Manners said that he always observed the regulations, but he had no idea when he took the car out that he had left his licence behind.

label: text
text: Regarding the serving of the summons, Mr. Manners thought it peculiar that it should have been done by a small Chinese boy. On it being pointed out that the Court Sergeant served summonses only when the drivers could not be found, His Worship remarked that the boy evidently knew Mr. Manners.

LANDLORD'S CLAIM.

label: paragraph_title
text: 一

label: text
text: Defendant counter-claimed for the same amount as money expended by him for the plaintiff's benefit and at the request of the plaintiff or his agent; or in the alternative being the amount of damage suffered by the defendant in consequence of a breach of agreement by the plaintiff.

label: text
text: A tenant, who deducted from his rent the sum of $210 incurred in expenditure on gas fittings for which it is alleged the landlord was liable, appeared at the Summary Court yesterday afternoon when the landlord claimed $210 as balance of rent due.

label: text
text: Plaintiff was to Sze-tuen, owner of 6-Kennedy Road, occupied by defendant (M. Albert Guetnt, proprietor of the Albert Cafe). Plaintiff was represented by Mr. W. B. Hind and Mr. L. D. Turner represented the defendant.

label: text
text: The Chinese rent collector gave evidence of receiving a cheque for $190 and two receipts for gas things when he called in June. This was in respect of a month's rent (of $400).

label: text
text: Questioned by His Honour witness said he considered this receipt as a discharge of the month's rent, $400. He was authorised by the landlord to make such discharge.

label: text
text: Chn Kn-po, who said he managed some of the affairs of the plaintiff, in cross-examination; admitted that after an inspection of the house by the defendant before he entered into occupation, the clause relative to fixtures was added.

label: text
text: The case was adjourned until Friday afternoon.

label: paragraph_title
text: NOT DULL!

label: paragraph_title
text: AMENITIES OF CHINA STATION.

label: text
text: WHY THE APPEAL

label: text
text: It is easy to understand, ob- serves the "Naval and Military Gazette," why the "China Station is so popular with young naval officers.

label: text
text: It seems to promise possibilities of adventure which other foreign stations lack. Only those who know Hongkong can realise what a fine city it really is, despite its depressing climate.

label: text
text: There is good sport to be had on the China Station, although in this respect the East Indies Station probably has a great deal more to offer. But it is to spirit of adventure that China really appeals.

label: text
text: Gun-running and slave-dhowing in the Persian Gulf have shrunk to very negligible dimensions these days, although doubtless always prepared to break out actively again if given the opportunity.

label: text
text: But when a man joins the Yangtze or West River Patrol he knows pretty well that life is not going to be very dull. There is plenty to be done, and plenty to do in looking for it.

label: paragraph_title
text: MOTOR OFFENCE

label: paragraph_title
text:
MISLED BY REMARKS ON
LICENCE.

label: text
text: Mr. H. E. Gardner was summoned before Mr. J. H. B. Nihill at the Kowloon Magistracy yesterday for taking his motor car past another vehicle in a controlled area.

label: text
text: EUROPEAN'S DEFENCE.

label: text
text: Evidence of the alleged offence was given by Traffic Sergeant Smith, who said that Mr. Gardner driving a motor car passed witness on his right side and also overtook a bus.

label: text
text: Pleading not guilty to the charge, Mr. Gardner denied that he passed the bus. He admitted that he overtook a motor cycle driven by a lady, as she appeared to be unsteady on her machine, and he thought it the safest thing to do was to get ahead. Further, Mr. Gardner pointed out the misleading nature of a section of the traffic regulations printed on the back of licences.

label: text
text: His Worship remarked that he found Mr. Gardner guilty of a technical offence, but in view of his defence he would caution him and bring the point to the notice of the C.S.P.

label: paragraph_title
text: BETTER PAY.

label: paragraph_title
text: AMERICA'S, ADVICE TO FRANCE.

label: text
text: OR MAY OWE MOVE.

label: text
text: Although officially ignoring George's Clemenceu's open letter to President Coolidge complaining of America's war's debt demands on France, the Washington authorities pointed out to day that if France fails to ratify the Mellon-Berenger agreement it will owe $407,000,000 in principal on its war supplies, debt in 1929. The war supplies purchased from America after the war while Clemenceu was premier, now bear five per cent. interest. Under the Mellon-Berenger settlement this obligation will be consolidated with other war debts, bearing a much lower rate of interest.—"Associated Press."

label: text
text: Secretary Mellon, who is now here to visit his daughter, said that he saw no reason for commenting on the open letter from ex-Premier Clemenceau of France to President Coolidge asking for tolerance toward the French debt. Only one paragraph of the letter was published in the newspapers of Rome and it aroused only slight comment.—"United Press."

label: paragraph_title
text:
AMERICA & RUBBER.
EXPERIMENTAL PLANTINGS
IN CUBA.

label: text
text: APPROPRIATIONS BEING MADE.

label: text
text:
O. F. Cokehead, member of the rubber section of the department of agriculture, is an route to Cuba to study experimental rubber plantings that have been made in several Cuban provinces, especially in Oriente, Camaguay and Guantanamo, which are believed best
Atted for rubber cultivation. A government station has been established in Santiago and many successful commercial varieties have been planted and their growth is being carefully studied.

label: text
text:
Little interest has hitherto been taken in rubber cultivation in Cuba, but the prospects for continued low price of sugar have led leading planters to consider branching out into other tropical and subtropical products. The nearness to the United States makes the field of particular value to America, where the market would be found. Both the Cuban and American governments have made appropriations for the work, which will be conducted under the immediate supervision of the department of agriculture.
Mr. Cokehead will stop en route in Florida, where about 20 varieties of rubber have been under cultivation for several years, in an effort to find a species that will thrive so far north as the Continental United States.

label: text
text: Secretary of Agriculture Jardine has been conferring with the Cuban minister to Washington during the past week with prospect of organising a Cuban-American rubber corporation. Secretary Jardine says that there are strong hopes that such a company will soon begin operations.—"United Press."

label: paragraph_title
text: MEXICAN REVOLT.

label: paragraph_title
text: NIPPED IN BUD ON U.S. TERRITORY.

label: text
text:
San Diego, Cal., August 16.
The American authorities have arrested and imprisoned 150 men, mobilised three miles on this side of the Mexican frontier, under command of General Enrique Estrada, Mexican ex-Secretary of War, when on the point of making an insurgent descent on towns across the border.

label: text
text: The captured include Estrada and his staff. The authorities also seized quantities of arms, an armoured truck, two one-ton truck loads of ammunition and lorries for transporting the revolutionaries; also documents giving complete plans of their projected insurrection.—Reuter's American Service.
